authoredPrompt: This figure contains two panels, labeled a) and b), each showing a three-dimensional surface plot of the supervised learning loss L[phi] as a function of two model parameters: the slope phi_1 (ranging from approximately -1.0 to 1.0) and the intercept phi_0 (ranging from approximately 0.0 to 2.0), with the vertical loss axis extending from 0 to 70. Panel a) renders the bowl-shaped quadratic loss landscape as a shaded 3D mesh surface, while panel b) shows the corresponding top-down 2D heatmap with contour lines over the same (phi_0, phi_1) plane; three circular markers (one pale gray-white, one light cyan, one teal) mark the same example parameter settings in both panels, and the minimum of the bowl — corresponding to the optimal parameter values — is visible in both views. The surface exhibits the characteristic smooth, convex shape of a least-squares regression loss, with the loss rising steeply as parameters deviate from the optimum in either direction. The figure introduces the loss landscape of a supervised linear model, illustrating that gradient-based optimization reliably converges to the global minimum because the surface has no local minima or saddle points.
authoredInteractions:
- Rotate the 3D loss surface in panel a: spin the L[φ] bowl over the slope φ1 (−1 to 1) and intercept φ0 (0 to 2) axes to inspect the curvature from any viewpoint, with the current parameter marker staying synchronized with the heatmap in panel b
- Drag the current parameter point on the surface: place (φ0, φ1) at any location on the bowl and trace an animated gradient-descent path of iterative steps descending toward the minimum, displaying the current loss value
- Slider for learning rate: change the step size and animate successive gradient-descent updates on the surface, showing overshooting and oscillation for large rates versus slow convergence for small rates

discrepancies: Panel (b) is rendered as a tilted plane in an isometric 3D view instead of a flat front-facing 2D plot
The entire generated scene is scaled far too small, occupying only a tiny portion of the viewport
Labels are severely overlapping into an illegible cluster due to the scaling issues
An interactive gradient descent path (yellow line) was added that does not exist in the source figure
The bounding box grid lines and tick marks for the axes are missing or poorly implemented
evaluation.notes: Excellent interactive pedagogical concept, but the visual execution is ruined by incorrect camera scale, overlapping labels, and forcing a 2D heatmap into a 3D isometric projection.
action_items: Increase the camera zoom or scale up the group geometries so the plots comfortably fill the viewport
Rotate panel (b) to face the camera directly, canceling out the isometric camera angle, or render it in a separate front-facing pass
Space out the labels and adjust their positions relative to the scaled geometry to prevent overlapping
plan_action_items: Do not use a global isometric camera setup (`axisScreenAngles`) for a figure that contains a strictly 2D panel; instead, use a standard front-facing orthographic camera and manually rotate the 3D plot group to achieve the isometric look while keeping the 2D panel flat.
